title: The nerve of a free product over a discrete object set
statement:
Let $O$ be a small set, let $I_O$ be its discrete category (only identity arrows), and let $D,E$ be small ordinary categories with object set $O$. Let $D*_O E$ denote their coproduct among categories with object set $O$ and functors equal to the identity on objects: its arrows are finite composable words in arrows from the two factors, modulo their internal composition and identity relations. Write $NC$ for the simplicial nerve of an ordinary category $C$, with $n$-simplices the strings of $n$ composable arrows, using simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Form the degreewise simplicial-set pushout $ND\amalg_{NI_O}NE$ along the identity-arrow inclusions. The canonical map
$$ND\amalg_{NI_O}NE\longrightarrow N(D*_O E)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. Neither factor is assumed free, connected or nonempty.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories (1980), Lemma 3.8 and its proof, printed pp.272-273 (PDF pp.6-7), with free product defined in Section 1.4(iii). No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: For a small directed graph $Q$ on $O$, let $P(Q)$ be its finite-edge-word category and let $K(Q)\subseteq NP(Q)$ be generated by the vertices and single edges. Apply [lem-coef-free-category-graph-nerve] to obtain the weak homotopy equivalence $K(Q)\hookrightarrow NP(Q)$. The lemma allows loops, repeated vertices, isolated objects and the empty graph, so it applies to each of the generating graphs used in step 2. This is the Proposition 2.9 input to the free case of Dwyer--Kan Lemma 3.8.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories (1980), Section 2.8 and Proposition 2.9 at k=1, printed p.271 (PDF p.5); Section 2.1 defines free categories. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Suppose $D=P(Q_D)$ and $E=P(Q_E)$ are free. Tag the edges from the two graphs to make them disjoint. A functor out of $P(Q_D\amalg_O Q_E)$ fixing $O$ is specified uniquely by the images of these edges, hence by a pair of functors out of $D,E$. Therefore $D*_O E=P(Q_D\amalg_O Q_E)$. Write $K_D,K_E,K$ for the three generating-graph simplicial subsets of step 1. Then $K=K_D\amalg_{NI_O}K_E$: the only simplices common to the two generating graphs are the identity strings at their vertices. The maps $NI_O\to K_D$ and $NI_O\to ND$ are monomorphisms, because each identity string remembers its object. Apply the pushout clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to the map of spans $(K_D\leftarrow NI_O\to K_E)\to(ND\leftarrow NI_O\to NE)$. Its component maps are the two weak equivalences of step 1 and the identity. It gives a weak equivalence $a:K\to ND\amalg_{NI_O}NE$. Step 1 also gives the weak equivalence $b:K\to N(D*_O E)$. If $j$ is the canonical map in the item, $ja=b$, since both composites are the inclusions on every vertex and generating edge. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] proves that $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for free $D,E$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2 and the first sentence of the proof of Lemma 3.8, printed pp.270,272: the free case from Proposition 2.9, with the generating-graph pushout comparison written out.

proof.text: For arbitrary $D,E$, use the free-category comonad and its augmented standard resolution defined in [lem-coef-free-resolution-coproduct-augmentation]. Put $X_q=F^{q+1}D$, $Y_q=F^{q+1}E$ for $q\geq0$, with the counit faces, comultiplication degeneracies and augmentations $\epsilon_X:X\to\operatorname{const}D$, $\epsilon_Y:Y\to\operatorname{const}E$ specified there. Each $X_q,Y_q$ is a small free category on $O$. Apply that node's mappingwise augmentation assertion with $A=I_O$, first to $C=D$ and then to $C=E$. Since $I_O*_O C=C$ and $I_O*_O F^{q+1}C=F^{q+1}C$ by the word presentation, this proves that $\epsilon_X,\epsilon_Y$ are weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set. The free-product invariance clause of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] now gives the same mappingwise assertion for $\epsilon_X*_O\epsilon_Y:X*_O Y\to\operatorname{const}(D*_O E)$. Its hypotheses require only simplicial categories on $O$ and mappingwise weak equivalences; no cofibrancy or freeness of $D,E$ is being inferred.

source.place: Sections 2.4-2.5, Propositions 2.6-2.7, and Lemma 3.8 proof (ii), printed pp.270-273: standard resolutions and mappingwise augmentation equivalences.

proof.text: For a simplicial category $A$ on $O$, write $\mathcal N(A)=\operatorname{diag}_{p,q}N_p(A_q)$. The local-weak-equivalence clause of [lem-coef-diagonal-coherent-nerve-comparison] applies to the three augmentation functors of step 3: they fix $O$ and are mappingwise weak homotopy equivalences. It gives weak homotopy equivalences $\alpha:\mathcal N(X)\to ND$, $\beta:\mathcal N(Y)\to NE$, and $v:\mathcal N(X*_O Y)\to N(D*_O E)$. Only that node's diagonal-nerve invariance clause is used; it imposes no Kan hypothesis. On the constant simplicial categories the displayed diagonals are exactly their ordinary nerves. Let $U=\mathcal N(X)\amalg_{NI_O}\mathcal N(Y)$ and $U_0=ND\amalg_{NI_O}NE$. In every degree the identity string still remembers its object, so $NI_O\to\mathcal N(X)$ and $NI_O\to ND$ are monomorphisms. The map of spans $(\alpha,1_{NI_O},\beta)$ therefore satisfies every hypothesis of the pushout clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences], giving a weak homotopy equivalence $u:U\to U_0$.

source.place: Section 1.4(vi)-(vii) and Lemma 3.8 proof (ii), printed pp.269,272-273: invariance of the diagonal nerve under mappingwise weak equivalences and the left vertical union map.

proof.text: Define bisimplicial sets $B_{p,q}=N_pX_q\amalg_{(NI_O)_p}N_pY_q$ and $T_{p,q}=N_p(X_q*_O Y_q)$. All operators of $B$ come from the degreewise pushout, and those of $T$ from the simplicial free product. The canonical inclusions of the two factors define a bisimplicial map $h:B\to T$: every operator commutes with it since both restrictions are the corresponding nerve maps of the factor functors. For each fixed $q$, the map $h_{\bullet,q}$ is the free-case comparison of step 2, since $X_q,Y_q$ are free. It is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence], using its permission to exchange the two directions, to obtain a weak homotopy equivalence $t:\operatorname{diag}B\to\operatorname{diag}T$. Degreewise, $(\operatorname{diag}B)_n=N_nX_n\amalg_{(NI_O)_n}N_nY_n=U_n$, and the simultaneous operators agree with those of $U$, so $\operatorname{diag}B=U$. Also $\operatorname{diag}T=\mathcal N(X*_O Y)$. Thus $t:U\to\mathcal N(X*_O Y)$ is the top horizontal weak equivalence in the source's resolution square. No natural choice of the horn pairing across the resolution is required: the row maps are the canonical inclusions, and it is these maps whose naturality was just verified.

source.place: Section 1.4(vii) and Lemma 3.8 proof (i), printed pp.269,272-273: apply the diagonal theorem to the degreewise free-case inclusions.

proof.text: Let $j:U_0\to N(D*_O E)$ be the map asserted in the item. The maps constructed above satisfy $ju=vt$. To check this equality in every simplicial degree, restrict to either factor $\mathcal N(X)$ or $\mathcal N(Y)$ of $U$. In the first case, both composites apply the augmentation of $X$ and then include $D$ into $D*_O E$; in the second, both apply the augmentation of $Y$ and then include $E$. These agree on $NI_O$ and the degreewise pushout property proves equality. Steps 4-5 make $u,v,t$ weak homotopy equivalences. Composition and two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore prove that the actual canonical map $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. All graphs, word sets, nerves and resolutions used here are small. If $O$ is empty all the nerves in the square are empty and the maps are identities; no step chooses a vertex. If a factor is $I_O$, its resolution and generating graph have only identity arrows. Loops, isolated vertices and disconnected categories were retained in the horn pairing and throughout the resolution square, so no extra nonemptiness or connectedness hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Conclusion of the commutative-diagram proof of Lemma 3.8, printed pp.272-273; commuting square and two-out-of-three written out.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 3.8, printed pp.272-273 (PDF pp.6-7), read from the scan; Sections 1.4(vi)-(vii), 2.1-2.9 supply its free-case and resolution inputs. The free-category generating-graph argument omitted in Proposition 2.9 is expanded here as explicit horn attachments; the proof follows the actual free-resolution square of Lemma 3.8.
